Blending a highly-weighted non-linear gradient boosting model with a heavily regularized Ridge regression captures both complex spatial patterns and global linear trends.

The pipeline incorporates advanced spatial feature engineering including Haversine metro and coastline distances, Gaussian RBF kernels over KMeans coordinate centroids, polar coordinates, and out-of-fold KNN spatial target aggregations.
insights: Constructing multi-scale spatial features and out-of-fold KNN target stats allows axis-aligned tree algorithms to effectively model continuous spatial housing markets. Combining complementary objective functions—such as log-target squared error and absolute loss alongside standard squared error—balances overall R2 variance explanation with reduced MAPE relative error on right-skewed target values.

description: The approach combines a 5-family ensemble featuring HistGradientBoostingRegressors trained on different target scales (raw, square-root, log1p) and loss functions (squared and absolute error), an MLP neural network, and Spline-Polynomial Ridge regression models. Final predictions are derived using SLSQP-optimized weights blending arithmetic and geometric ensemble averages.
insights: Continuous spatial representations are substantially enriched using piecewise-linear California coastline geometry, out-of-fold k-NN neighborhood price quantiles, and multi-scale Gaussian RBF kernel spatial estimators. Permutation-based feature selection efficiently prunes redundant variables, retaining the top features for non-linear spline and polynomial expansions.

description: The solution employs a 5-fold ensemble using HistGradientBoostingRegressor with three distinct target-loss heads per fold (raw target L2, log-target L2, and log-target L1) combined via arithmetic-geometric OOF blending. Features are enhanced through spatial coordinate rotations, distance metrics to major cities/coasts, and fold-isolated anisotropic directional and socio-structural kNN neighborhood aggregations.
insights: Training separate heads on raw L2 loss, log L2 loss, and log L1 loss balances the competing optimization targets of R² and MAPE. Directional neighborhood features (e.g., coastal-inland gradients) and multi-scale Gaussian kernel spatial smoothing provide rich local context without introducing data leakage.

description: The solution implements a 5-fold cross-validated ensemble of HistGradientBoostingRegressors trained under three complementary loss and scale formulations: raw-scale squared error, log-scale squared error, and log-scale absolute error. Predictions are combined using convex blend weights optimized on out-of-fold performance to simultaneously improve R², Pearson correlation, and MAPE.
insights: Constructing out-of-fold socio-spatial neighborhood aggregations via k-NN and kernel smoothing captured fine-grained local price dynamics without target leakage. Ensembling models trained with different loss functions directly addresses the trade-off between minimizing percentage errors on lower-value blocks and explaining total variance across top-coded target distributions.

description: The solution extracts spatial KNN neighborhood statistics and engineered socioeconomic density ratios, then fits a 5-fold cross-validated blend of two HistGradientBoostingRegressors—one trained on raw target values and the other on log1p-transformed target values. Predictions are bounded within domain limits ($14,999 to $500,001) and combined using an OOF-optimized blending weight.
insights: Combining models trained on raw and log-transformed targets balances overall variance explanation (R2) with relative percentage error (MAPE). Spatial KNN features, such as local mean income and target statistics, effectively capture local housing sub-market dynamics.

description: A 5-fold hybrid ensemble combining multi-objective HistGradientBoosting (trained on raw L2, log L2, and log L1 targets), a Multi-Layer Perceptron on quantile-normalized features, and a spline-expanded Ridge linear model. Spatial domain knowledge is integrated using out-of-fold KNN neighborhood target statistics, coastal/urban distance metrics, coordinate rotations, and top-coding ($500k ceiling) boundary calibration.
insights: Leveraging out-of-fold KNN and Gaussian spatial aggregations captures localized real estate sub-markets while preventing target leakage. Blending models trained under different loss functions and target scale representations alongside an explicit boundary classifier significantly improves performance across R2, MAPE, and Pearson metrics on capped, right-skewed data.

description: An ensemble of three HistGradientBoostingRegressor models trained on raw L2, log1p L2, and log1p L1 target loss formulations to balance R2 variance explanation and MAPE percentage error. The predictions are combined through Nelder-Mead optimization to calibrate arithmetic and geometric blends using out-of-fold neighborhood context features.
insights: Constructing out-of-fold KD-tree aggregations across both pure geographic coordinates and joint geo-socioeconomic spaces provides rich regional market context. Diversifying loss functions (L1 vs. L2) and target scales (raw vs. log1p) allows individual models to target specific metrics before being optimally blended for composite multi-metric objectives.

description: This approach uses a multi-architecture 5-fold cross-validation ensemble combining HistGradientBoosting models trained with distinct loss functions (raw L2, log L2, and log L1) alongside out-of-fold Ridge spline models and an ExtraTrees regressor. Extensive geographic engineering is incorporated, including multi-scale KNN smoothed spatial target statistics, piecewise coastline geometry, and unsupervised sub-market clustering.
insights: Rich spatial context features—such as continuous distance to coastline polylines, exponential distance kernels, and local KNN neighborhood target summaries—significantly enhance price estimation across distinct micro-markets. Combining models trained on both raw dollar scale (optimizing R²) and log-transformed target scale (optimizing MAPE), followed by post-processing low-tail damping and top-code capping, delivers strong overall performance.

description: The pipeline employs an ensemble of raw-scale and log-transformed HistGradientBoostingRegressors trained on engineered features, including coastline/bay geometry, B-spline basis projections, and multi-scale k-NN spatial context. Out-of-fold Ridge regression models fitted on B-spline surfaces provide smooth prior estimates and spatial residual kriging signals to the gradient boosted trees.
insights: Constructing coastal-anisotropic k-NN sectors and continuous coastline geometry effectively models sharp price gradients along California sub-markets (e.g., coastal vs. inland). Blending predictions from models trained on raw dollar targets and log-transformed targets balances global R² variance explanation with lower relative percentage error (MAPE).

description: The approach uses a 5-fold cross-validated ensemble of HistGradientBoostingRegressor models trained across four distinct target scales (raw MSE, Box-Cox power MSE, log1p MSE, and log1p MAE) to optimize R2 and MAPE jointly. Inputs are enhanced with quantile B-spline basis expansions, out-of-fold Ridge spline regression, coordinate rotations, metro distance metrics, and multi-scale out-of-fold KNN spatial context.
insights: Transforming the right-skewed target into logarithmic and power spaces enables simultaneous optimization for relative error (MAPE) and overall variance (R2). Combining arithmetic and geometric prediction averages tuned via Nelder-Mead optimization, along with target ceiling boundary snapping ($500,000), effectively captures local spatial autocorrelation while resolving top-coded data artifacts.

insights: Injecting spatial context via local out-of-fold KNN neighborhood statistics and explicit distance-to-coastline geometry dramatically improves real estate price estimation in complex regional micro-markets.
